questions: What is the exact definition of a "good string" in terms of its relationship to sequence A and the operations?
Are the operations applied sequentially on the current state of A, or is A reset to its original state for each operation?
Can the indices i wrap around the sequence boundaries when performing the operations?
Is the string S fixed throughout the process, or can it be modified during the operations?
What happens if N is less than 3, given that the operations require checking three consecutive positions?
Are duplicate operations (same i value) allowed, or can each position only be used once?
Does the existence of a good string depend on being able to make A contain no 0s in a finite number of operations, or is there a specific limit?
How should overlapping operations be handled when they affect the same positions in sequence A?
answers: A string S makes A good if repeatedly applying the described operations can turn every element of A into 1, as stated.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume operations are applied sequentially, each acting on the current (possibly already-modified) state of A.
Only as given by the stated wraparound definitions (S_{N+1}=S_1, S_{N+2}=S_2, A_{N+1}=A_1); not specified further.
S is fixed once chosen; only A is modified by the operations.
Not applicable; N is guaranteed to be at least 3.
Not specified beyond 'any number of times, possibly zero,' which allows repeating operations on the same or overlapping indices.
A finite number of operations suffices if achievable at all, since each operation only ever sets values to 1, never back to 0.
Not specified beyond what's given; operations may be applied in any order and can affect overlapping positions since 'any number of times' places no ordering restriction.
inline_prompts: You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of length N, consisting of 0 and 1. We call a string S of length N, a good string if it is possible to perform the following operation any number of times (possibly zero) so that the sequence A contains no 0. Here, S_i (1\leq i\leq N) denotes the i-th character of S, and we define S_{N+1}=S_1, S_{N+2}=S_2, and A_{N+1}=A_1. A string S makes A good if repeatedly applying the described operations can turn every element of A into 1, as stated. - Perform one of the following operations: - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_i= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_{i+2}= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with 1. - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_{i+2}= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_i= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with 1. Determine whether there exists a good string. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output If there exists a good string, print Yes; otherwise, print No. The judge is case-insensitive; for example, if the correct answer is Yes, outputs such as yes, YES, or yEs will also be accepted. Constraints - 3\leq N\leq 200000 - A_i\in \lbrace 0,1 \rbrace (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
